rules: Quote exactly; never paraphrase inside quotation marks.
A card praises the work, never Tinct or its edition.
No photos or likenesses of the people quoted.
Only cards with recheck == 'verified' may be sent to readers.

cards.label: Read by
cards.quote: Formerly Milton's ‘Paradise Lost’ had been my chief favourite, and in my excursions during the voyage of the ‘Beagle,’ when I could take only a single volume, I always chose Milton.
cards.context: Autobiography, in The Life and Letters of Charles Darwin (1887 text)
cards.qualification: 'Formerly' is his: he later writes he 'cannot endure to read a line of poetry'. Present it as his Beagle companion, never as a lifelong favourite. Use this 1887 text only (the 1958 Barlow edition adds 'small').

cards.label: Kept by
cards.quote: he constantly laid Homer's Iliads, according to the copy corrected by Aristotle, called the casket copy, with his dagger under his pillow, declaring that he esteemed it a perfect portable treasure of all military virtue and knowledge.
cards.context: Plutarch, Life of Alexander, tr. John Dryden, reporting Onesicritus
cards.qualification: Present as 'Plutarch reports, citing Onesicritus, that Alexander…'. Never as Alexander's own words.

cards.label: Read by
cards.quote: I had long ago read Jane Austen's Sense and Sensibility, and now I thought I would have Pride and Prejudice.
cards.context: His memoirs, recovering from illness and fever at Carthage, December 1943; Sarah read it aloud
cards.qualification: The archive page doesn't say 'pneumonia'; don't add it. Also usable: 'I had always thought it would be better than its rival.' / 'Sarah read it to me beautifully from the foot of the bed.'

why_read_old_books.quote: Any book that survived for two thousand years has been filtered through many people.
why_read_old_books.qualification: Eric Jorgenson's edited compilation of Naval, not a verbatim transcript; label as 'The Almanack of Naval Ravikant'.

why_read_old_books.quote: But I really think people should be much more biased towards older books than they are.
why_read_old_books.qualification: He means books up to ~10 years old (example: The Dream Machine, 2001), not the classics. Using it for classics misrepresents him.

why_read_old_books.quote: You could spend your entire life only reading timeless works which is what smart people used to do.
We all, therefore, need the books that will correct the characteristic mistakes of our own period.
why_read_old_books.context: Introduction to Athanasius, On the Incarnation

why_read_old_books.quote: For what are the classics but the noblest recorded thoughts of man?
